First time, Tuesday, 18:30 to 21:00

Spoon carving from a green log

The whole evening is one object. You start with a length of wood that was a branch a fortnight ago, and you leave with a spoon that you will use, lose, and be quietly pleased about for years.

  • TutorNour Haddad
  • LevelFirst time, no experience at all
  • Benches4 of 10 free
  • Fee18 pounds, an illustrative example
01

What to bring

Which is, mostly, nothing.

  • Nothing sharp

    Every knife, axe and hook knife in the room belongs to the workshop and stays in the room. Bringing your own is fine but it gets checked first.

  • Clothes you can ruin

    Green wood is wet and it stains. Aprons hang by the door. Shoes have to cover your whole foot.

  • Nothing, we have those

    Safety glasses and a cut resistant glove for your holding hand are handed out at the start and counted back in at the end.

  • Something to write on

    Optional, and about half the room does it. The grain does not care but you will want to remember which way it ran.

What you will make

One eating spoon, about the length of your hand, with a shallow bowl and a handle that suits whichever way you hold it. It will be slightly crooked. That is not a fault of the evening, it is a property of spoons.

You will also leave with a bag of shavings if you want them, a blunted edge you sharpened yourself, and a fairly strong opinion about birch.

The rest of the programme
02

The shape of the evening

Two and a half hours, and it does run over.

  1. 18:30

    Split a log

    Birch or cherry, cut this month, split down with a froe until you have a billet the size of your forearm.

  2. 18:50

    Axe out the blank

    Ten minutes of demonstration at the front, then the chopping block. This is the loud part of the evening.

  3. 19:30

    Knife work

    The outside shape first, then the crank, then the handle. Sitting down, elbows in, thumb behind the blade.

  4. 20:20

    Hollow the bowl

    Hook knife, both hands, short strokes across the grain. Everybody goes through the bottom at least once in their first year.

  5. 20:50

    Sweep up and go

    Tools wiped and back on the wall, shavings in the yard bin, spoon in your pocket. It dries over a fortnight.

Your tutor

Nour has taught this evening more times than anybody has counted and still splits the logs herself on the afternoon of the class, because green wood that has sat about for a week carves like a chair leg.
